# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.

शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).

Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

items.t: Bihar gives one woman in every family Rs 10,000 to start work of her own choice, such as a small shop, tailoring, a beauty parlour, an e-rickshaw, or goat, poultry or cow rearing. She must be a member of a JEEViKA self-help group, or join one; in villages the form is handed in at the JEEViKA village organisation (Gram Sangathan), which approves it and sends it up for payment. Once the work has started it is reviewed, and further help of up to Rs 2 lakh is given in stages. The second instalment of Rs 20,000 is being paid in 2026 to women whose first Rs 10,000 was checked and found properly used.
Rs 10,000 first instalment, then up to Rs 2 lakh more after review
One woman per family. A family means husband, wife and their unmarried children; an unmarried adult woman whose parents have both died counts as a family of her own
Aged 18 to 60 years and living in Bihar
A member of a JEEViKA self-help group. A woman outside a group can join one by giving a self-declaration at the Gram Sangathan along with her application
Neither the woman nor her husband pays income tax
Neither the woman nor her husband is in government service, whether regular or contract
Bank passbook of a working savings account in her own name, linked to her Aadhaar
Name of her JEEViKA self-help group and Gram Sangathan
Self-declaration form (Annexure-2), only if she is not yet in a self-help group

In a village: at the meeting or office of your JEEViKA Mahila Gram Sangathan (village organisation). Ask your self-help group's Community Mobiliser (CM) or the Gram Sangathan president for the free application form (Annexure-1), fill it in, tick the business you want to start, sign it and hand it in there with photocopies of your Aadhaar and bank passbook. If you are not in a group yet, give the self-declaration form (Annexure-2) at the same place so that you are added to one. In a town: apply on JEEViKA's urban Mahila Rojgar Yojana portal (mmry.brlps.in, linked from brlps.in) when it is open, or ask the urban self-help group office of your municipality. No fee is charged anywhere, and no agent is needed.
To the President, Jeevika Mahila Gram Sangathan
Laxmi Jeevika Mahila Gram Sangathan, Basantpur, panchayat Mohiuddinpur, block Paroo, district Muzaffarpur
The village organisation that your self-help group belongs to. Your Community Mobiliser will tell you its exact name.
Your full name, spelt exactly as on your Aadhaar card.
Write your husband's name if you are married, otherwise your father's.
General, Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Extremely Backward Class or Backward Class.
The place where you live now.
Self-help group (Jeevika Mahila Swayam Sahayata Samuh)
Durga Jeevika Mahila Swayam Sahayata Samuh, Basantpur
The name of your own group. If you have just given the self-declaration to join, write the group you are being added to.
State Bank of India, 3999 0012 3456, Paroo branch, SBIN0009999
Your own savings account, linked to Aadhaar. Copy the IFSC from the passbook; the money is sent to this account by DBT.
Your 12-digit Aadhaar number. The JEEViKA block office enters it on the portal, so check every digit.
Members in the family (male / female)
Count husband, wife and unmarried children living as one family.
Business you want to start (tick one)
Pick one from the list of 18 on the second page, for example kirana shop, vegetable stall, tailoring, beauty parlour, e-rickshaw, goat, poultry or cow rearing, or write your own.

Meet your self-help group's Community Mobiliser or the Gram Sangathan president and take the free application form. If you are not in a JEEViKA group, fill the self-declaration form too so that you are added to one.
Fill in your name, family, group, bank account and Aadhaar details, tick the business you want to start, sign, and hand the form in at the Gram Sangathan with copies of your Aadhaar and passbook.
The Gram Sangathan holds a special meeting, approves the eligible applications and sends them to the JEEViKA block office, which enters each one on its MIS portal with the Aadhaar number.
The JEEViKA district office checks the list and JEEViKA headquarters sends Rs 10,000 by DBT to your Aadhaar-linked bank account. Check your passbook or ask at the bank or CSC.
Start the work you chose and keep the bills for what you buy. JEEViKA staff come to see how it is going and arrange training.
After the review, women whose work is running get the next instalment (Rs 20,000 in 2026) and later more help, up to Rs 2 lakh in all, in stages.
Your self-help group's Community Mobiliser or the JEEViKA block office (BPIU); JEEViKA state office, Patna: 0612-2504980
Diesel Anudan Yojana (Bihar Diesel Subsidy for Irrigation)
Agriculture Department, Government of Bihar (Directorate of Agriculture)

When the monsoon fails and farmers have to water kharif crops with diesel pump sets, Bihar pays back part of the diesel cost: Rs 75 a litre, counted as Rs 750 an acre for each watering. Farmers registered on the DBT Agriculture portal upload the computerised petrol-pump receipt and apply online, and the money goes to their Aadhaar-linked bank account. The 2026-27 kharif round was ordered on 10 August 2026 and covers the districts the state named as short of rain; each year the list of districts is shown on the application page.
Rs 750 an acre per watering, up to Rs 2,250 an acre, for up to 8 acres
Registered on the DBT Agriculture portal with a 13-digit number, and a bank account linked to Aadhaar and NPCI
Owner farmers, sharecroppers (bataidar), or both, in villages or towns of the covered districts
Paddy nursery and jute: up to 2 waterings (Rs 1,500 an acre). Standing paddy, maize, pulses, oilseeds, vegetables and medicinal plants: up to 3 waterings (Rs 2,250 an acre)
Diesel bought for irrigation from a registered petrol pump in Bihar, between the start date and the last date of the scheme
One applicant per family (husband, wife and minor children), for at most 8 acres; the least paid is Rs 100
Computerised or digital receipt from the petrol pump, with the last 10 digits of your registration number written on it and your signature or thumb mark
For owner farmers: rent receipt (lagan rasid) or LPC issued in 2023-24, 2024-25 or 2025-26
For sharecroppers: the prescribed form signed jointly by a ward member, mukhiya, sarpanch or panchayat samiti member and the Krishi Samanvayak
Thana, khata and khesra numbers of the field watered, and the names of two neighbouring farmers
Mobile number registered on the portal, for the OTP
Anudan ka prakar (type of subsidy)
Choose the diesel subsidy application from the list.
Your 13-digit DBT Agriculture registration number. Your name and bank details appear by themselves.

Krishi Input Anudan Yojana (Bihar DBT Kisan Registration)

When floods, heavy rain, drought or hail destroy more than a third of a crop, Bihar pays farmers in the notified panchayats an input subsidy for each hectare lost, straight into the bank. To get this, or any other farm subsidy such as diesel, seed or machines, a farmer first registers once on the DBT Agriculture portal and gets a 13-digit registration number. The latest round, for crops lost in the floods of August and September 2026, took applications in October 2026; a new round opens after each notified disaster, usually for about a week.
Rs 8,500 a hectare (rain-fed), Rs 17,000 (irrigated), Rs 22,500 (perennial crops), up to 2 hectares

Register once: open dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in, click Kisan Panjikaran, verify your Aadhaar, fill in your farmer, land and bank details and note the 13-digit registration number. The block agriculture office (e-Kisan Bhawan) does it free; a CSC or Vasudha Kendra can also do it.
After a flood or drought, check the panchayat list on the portal. If your panchayat is listed, open Krishi Input Anudan under online services within the dates shown, usually about a week.

Enter the 13-digit number, choose your farmer type, fill in the total and damaged land in decimal, the thana-khata-khesra numbers and two neighbours' names, enter the captcha and the OTP, upload the rent receipt, LPC or certified self-declaration, and submit. The application number comes by SMS.

The Krishi Samanvayak visits the field within 2 to 4 days, photographs the plot and forwards or rejects the claim with a reason. The sub-divisional and district agriculture officers and the district disaster officer then approve it.

Bihar Building Workers Registration (BOCW Labour Card)
Bihar Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Resources Department, Government of Bihar

Masons, labourers, carpenters, painters, plumbers and other construction workers who register with the Bihar BOCW Welfare Board get a labour card that opens more than a dozen benefits: Rs 50,000 for a daughter's marriage, maternity and paternity money, a bicycle grant, help with children's studies, Rs 3,000 a year for medical costs, a Rs 1,000 monthly pension at 60, and Rs 2 to 4 lakh to the family if the worker dies. Registration is done online with Aadhaar on the board's portal, or at a CSC or the block labour office. The fee is small: Rs 20 for registration plus the membership fee, Rs 50 in all for five years.

Mukhyamantri Jan Arogya Yojana Bihar (Ayushman Card for Ration Card Holders)
Bihar Swasthya Suraksha Samiti, Health Department, Government of Bihar, with the National Health Authority

Bihar pays for the same free hospital cover of Rs 5 lakh a year as Ayushman Bharat for ration-card families that the central PM-JAY list left out. Since 2024 every family holding an NFSA ration card in Bihar is covered, either under PM-JAY or under this state scheme, and both use the same Ayushman card at any empanelled hospital. The card is made free with the ration card and Aadhaar, on the Ayushman app or website, at a CSC, or at camps held at ration shops.
Rs 5 lakh a year per family, cashless, at empanelled hospitals
The family holds a Bihar ration card under the National Food Security Act (priority household or Antyodaya)
Families already on the central PM-JAY list are covered by PM-JAY; the other ration-card families are covered by this state scheme, with the same card
Every member named on the ration card is covered, with no limit on family size or age
Illnesses you already have are covered from the first day
Each member needs his or her own card, made after Aadhaar e-KYC
